questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Administratively relatively easy destination, interest in the local culture and language, relevant and interesting sounding courses at host university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I had a really great time, but would have loved to be even more immersed in the local culture - international students were a bit "apart" here. 
Interesting classes, but very strict with grading and exams. High study load.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introduction week, including how to guides and presentations on everything practical as well as faculty-related academic stuff.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used Kotwijs, and started as soon as I knew I was definitely going. It was quite easy to find something, and there were several different opportunities available still when I was searching

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you live with Belgian students, you will be alone a lot during the weekends, as they usually go home. Doing laundry at laundromats is expensive. It's really fun t ohave housemates if you get to know them a bit!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register via their online tool, KU Loket. You then have two weeks to try out the classes before you have to finalize your registration, which is quite nice!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: In the introweek it was arranged so that an administrative advisor guided all the internationals at the faculty, in person, on how to sign up. She went around and helped as well, and she was super helpful and quick to respond over mail too.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very, got everything I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make use of the two week window where you can try out different classes, but don't go overboard - those classes still matter, and you have to prepare for them, take notes, and potentially do assignments for them, so it's a lot of work if you do a lot of extra ones.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: On the level I was expecting from MA courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less class discussions, but otherwise pretty comparable. More graded assignments/tests/presentations than I was used to for some classes

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The Low Countries at the Crossroads of European History
Translation and Plurilingualism in Literature
Language Varieties and Language Variants
Taal en onderwijs: sociolinguïstische aspecten
Humor en creativiteit in taal

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I'm glad I took The Low Countries at the Crossroads of European History: Learning about the history of the area gave a lot of context for when I then went out and visited other towns and places in the country. 

Taal en onderwijs and Humor en creaitiviteit in taal were both cool, smaller classes, and it really boosted my Dutch that I took those. If you have (close to) a B1 in Dutch, following along is doable, and my profs were very accomodating in letting me write my final papers in English.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Laundromats are expensive (6,5 eur ish per machine, 4 for drying). 
Trains to go to other cities can get quite expensive if you go on a lot of trips.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Coffee and beer are way less expensive than in Copenhagen (unless you go to the very trendy places).
Busses are quite affordable (a 10-trip ticket cost 22 eur).
Sportscard is really cheap, especially considering how much you gain access to with it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different sports (can also be seen on their website). Faculty bars and Pangaea, the international cafe/hub/space were nice and cheap social spaces.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The bar Blauwe Kater has free live blues concerts every Monday, always a vibe.
STUK has a lot of cool events (movie showings, open mics, concerts, art etc).
In general make sure to go out a lot - pub crawls, Faculty Bar events, Oude Markt, and the ESN parties too, were so fun, especially since so many other (international) students were also all in on it.
Go see the university choir perform if you have the opportunity, they're really good!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Antwerp, Gent and Brussels are super worth the visits. Really good art-, fashion- and architecture museums. Look into getting the belgian Museum Pass if you know you want to visit a good handful.
Super super good bike infrastructure between towns/cities, recommend going on rides. Leuven is quite small, so you're in the contryside in no time. + if you come in spring, then go check out a bike race, great atmosphere around it, a lot of local hype (Ronde van Vlaanderen f.x. starts in Antwerp)
There are over a thousand caves in Belgium?! Mostly in Wallonia, but worth the trip.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, not that different from back home

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to get to know people in your courses, and be persistent - local students are mostly super nice but are mostly not really on the look out for international friends, so it takes a while to get to know them. If you have Belgian housemates then try to reach out to them yourself.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
It seems like people work and study more independently here - I'm not used to sitting and studying in silence in the library for hours and hours every day.
Local students going home every weekend made it hard to become close with them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The laid back bar- and going out culture
Chilling outside as soon as the weather was just slightly okay 
There was a "serious" academic vibe about the uni, which I appreciated

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It's an academically challenging destination - there is definitely time to have fun and go on trips and such, but people can and do fail exams regularly here.
People will say you don't need to know Dutch to come here, and it's true, but if you learn some, even just a little, it allows you to learn about and participate in so many more cultural events - theater, concerts, movies, exhibitions etc - that are not advertized in English. It also makes you feel more integrated when you can use simple phrases in daily life, and language lessons, if you take them, are good and really fun.
Get extra salt for your fries at the frituurs, I swear they chronically undersalt them here.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a bike, the town is super bik friendly and really not that big. And unless you live in the opposite end of town from your campus, the Leuven bus pass is a waste of money (it's also gonna cost you money on top of the price of the card to get photos taken and the card made).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many new people, both locals and internationals. Having so much time on my hands to explore and go out and structure my days differently than I do back home. Living in a place that is truly a student town.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping up with coursework while also wanting to go on a lot of fun trips and activities.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
